links.note: The separation of powers and the checks and balances it provides, so that each organ can check what the other is doing - this concept's own explanation. Already linked and correct.
Dr. Kalam's position being nominal yet allowing him to impact countless lives - this concept draws that conclusion itself. Already linked and correct.
Democracy as the rule of the people, and whether all people can actually rule - this concept asks that question in those words and answers it with the class representative.
Comparing the class representative with elected members - this concept builds the whole idea of representation from the class monitor chosen by those they speak for. Already linked and correct.
Grassroots democracy enabling and encouraging the participation of ordinary citizens, who can then have a say in decisions that affect them - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
Demos meaning people and kratos meaning rule or power, so democracy literally means the rule of the people - this concept's etymology.
Why all people cannot rule directly - this concept answers that it is clearly not possible, and uses the impracticality of a whole class visiting the principal to show why.
The class monitor or class representative whom the whole class elected, sent to the principal on the class's behalf - this concept's analogy for representation. Already linked and correct.

Elected members discussing laws, problems and solutions in the assemblies and trying to convince each other through dialogue and debate - this concept's description, which makes the assembly a place of persuasion.
India as a representative democracy, where people vote for MLAs at the state level and MPs at the national level - this concept's statement.
All Indian citizens above the age of 18 having the right to participate in elections - this concept's rule, which is what makes the voter figure as large as it is.
Grassroots democracy as a system that enables and encourages the participation of ordinary citizens - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
Citizens having a say in the laws and rules governing society - this concept's closing point, which is what separates being ruled from taking part. Already linked and correct.
F.A.I.L. as First Attempt In Learning - one of the sayings this concept quotes from Dr. Kalam.
The state assembly or Vidhan Sabha at the state level - this concept's table, with the note that most states have a single assembly.
Rules necessary to maintain order and harmony because disagreements and disorder arise when many people live together - this concept's opening.
Governance as a process and government as the group or system that performs it - this concept's two definitions, which it is careful to distinguish. Already linked and correct.
Digital transfers replacing money orders and demand drafts, and the new class of criminals that followed - this concept's account of the change and the cybercrime it produced.
The legislature making new laws and sometimes updating or removing existing ones, through an assembly of representatives - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
The executive implementing or executing the laws, including the head of state, the ministers and enforcement agencies - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
The judiciary deciding whether the law has been broken and what course of action follows, and examining executive decisions and legislation - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, renowned scientist, 11th President of India and the Missile Man of India - this concept's profile.

Dr. Kalam as scientist, President and the Missile Man of India - this concept's profile. Already linked and correct. Note: this item duplicates the preceding one and its printed answer belongs to a different question, about technology driving new laws.
Dream is not that which you see while sleeping, it is something that does not let you sleep - this concept quotes that saying among Dr. Kalam's.
The two introductory pictures - this concept's LET'S EXPLORE asks the reader to describe them, say what differences they see and connect that with the discussion on rules. Already linked and correct.

Shopkeepers challenging a state law as unfair, and a court striking it down - this concept is where the judiciary examines whether a law is well conceived and fair to all, as part of the checks and balances. Already linked and correct.

A student council of class representatives carrying the students' case to the management - this concept's own analogy for representation, down to the detail that one representative is sent rather than the whole class. Already linked and correct.
